name: Bolsonarism
summary: Bolsonarism is the Brazilian far-right movement built around Jair Bolsonaro, combining economic liberalism, militarism and tough-on-crime politics, evangelical-backed moral conservatism, strong anti-communism and hostility to the left, 'globalism', the press and universities. Scholars describe it as a convergence of reactionary culture politics, militarism and ultraliberalism, with a personality cult and authoritarian tendencies.
scope: Bolsonarism as a movement from the 2018 Bolsonaro campaign through his presidency (2019-2022) and aftermath, based on the 2018 government plan, Bolsonaro's documented positions and scholarly analyses (Araujo and Carvalho). Follows the mainstream Bolsonarista core, not the Olavo de Carvalho ideological fringe, and many answers on non-Brazilian issues are inferred.

sources.usedFor: Report on the contents of the 2018 government plan: privatization, pensions, labor, security, guns, property.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Bolsonarism's economic liberalism and COVID-era stance favour private initiative and spending cuts, though adherents do not attack the existing universal SUS; inferred, not stated.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The ultraliberal, fiscally austere economic program favours restraint on wage floors and labor costs; inferred from the Guedes agenda.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Campaigning on deregulation, privatization and spending cuts under a liberal economist shows a pro-market preference, though critics say practice was less liberal.

public-ownership.rationale: The 2018 plan launched a broad privatization program to pay down debt and blamed past state "dirigismo" for recession.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: It campaigned on tax cuts for businesses and inheritances and a simpler, lighter tax system.

unions-good.rationale: The plan declined to restore the mandatory union tax and let individual contracts override the CLT, signalling hostility to union power.

property-fundamental.rationale: The plan proposed removing any qualification of property rights from the Constitution and treating land invasions as terrorism.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Deregulation and a liberal economy are central to its economic program.

cut-welfare.rationale: Split: the plan kept Bolsa Familia and proposed a minimum income via negative income tax, while the ultraliberal wing wants cuts.

worker-ownership.rationale: Bolsonarism is anti-communist and neoliberal, treating collective ownership as leftist; inferred from that framing.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Its security agenda stresses intelligence and technology for policing and law and order; terrorism-specific surveillance is inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The positions article says he opposed drug liberalisation and warned that a child who mixes with marijuana users will end up snorting cocaine.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents frame limits on speech as left-wing censorship and attack courts that police online speech.

strong-leader.rationale: The movement is built around a personality cult of the "myth" and hostility to Congress gridlock and institutions.

state-harmful.rationale: Ultraliberal rhetoric but combined with strong militarism and a strong security state, so not anti-statist.

limit-guns.rationale: The plan sought to ease carry permits by amending the disarmament statute and Bolsonaro defends self-defense rights.

empower-police-military.rationale: The plan offers police legal protection, tougher sentencing and tech funding; militarism is a component of the ideology.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Defense of traditional morality implies opposition; no specific source on sex work.

decide-locally.rationale: Plan decentralizes some taxes to municipalities, but the movement is nationalist and centralizing on security; split.

rehabilitation.rationale: The plan ends progressive sentencing and prison leave, favouring punishment.

traditional-family.rationale: Defending the traditional family and Christian values is a core pillar.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The positions article describes Bolsonaro as a vocal opponent of same-sex marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: The positions article lists abortion among the policies he vocally opposes and describes him as an anti-abortion politician.

more-religion-public.rationale: In 2017 he said the state is Christian and minorities must adapt, and he opposes state secularism, though in the 2018 campaign he promised to govern for everyone regardless of religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: He criticised university racial quotas as dividing society and opposes affirmative action.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Implied: Bolsonarism blames feminist and LGBTQ movements for moral chaos and defends the traditional family.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Patriotism and national flag symbolism are central.

gradual-change.rationale: It claims to defend traditional institutions yet attacks courts and elections and seeks rupture with the left; mixed, leaning to disagreement.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Bolsonaro opposes immigration, especially from Haiti, Africa and the Middle East.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Bolsonarism opposes globalism, which clearly implies resisting stronger international bodies; the source does not name the UN.

free-trade.rationale: He backed EU-Mercosur and US ties but also nationalist rhetoric toward China; split.

nation-first.rationale: Bolsonaro opposed globalism and worked with nationalist allies abroad, which implies putting national interest ahead of global cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anti-globalist, sovereignty-minded outlook; inferred, though alignment with the US/Israel muddies it.

open-borders.rationale: He opposed immigration, especially from Haiti, Africa and the Middle East, once calling such migrants the scum of humanity.

limit-growth.rationale: Rejects climate science and facilitated Amazon deforestation in favour of growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He rejects the scientific consensus and threatened to leave the Paris Agreement.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No stated position; scientific denialism sits beside pro-business modernization.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Advisers planned to expand nuclear and hydro power.

revolution-justified.rationale: Anti-left and pro-order, but adherents' January 8 insurrection and self-coup planning show some acceptance of rupture; split leaning no.

experts-over-public.rationale: Bolsonarism is associated with scientific denialism and sought to dismantle expert bodies such as the Oswaldo Cruz Foundation as dens of leftism.

central-planning.rationale: The plan blames state dirigismo for inflation and recession.

socialized-markets.rationale: Anti-communist and neoliberal, so rejects socialized ownership even in market form.

land-value-tax.rationale: Plan stresses tax simplification and cuts, not land taxes; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: It campaigned on cutting inheritance taxes.

basic-income.rationale: The plan proposed a minimum income via negative income tax, though conditional framing and ultraliberal opposition make adherents split.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Mixed: pro-trade-deal rhetoric but nationalist; no clear tariff doctrine.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The plan criticizes dirigismo and favours privatization over state-led industrial policy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Defends property and rural interests but opposed land reform; split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Implied by its anti-communism and the plan's market programme of privatisation and a new work card; abolishing money is never discussed.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The 2018 plan keeps a Central Bank that is formally and politically independent, alongside a new Economy Ministry.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Plan favours individual contracts and choice among unions over state-recognized bargaining.

one-party-rule.rationale: It competes in elections under a nationalist banner and sees the left as the threat, though critics call it authoritarian.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Republican movement; some monarchist sympathizers but not a stated position.

democracy-best.rationale: Adherents proclaim defense of democracy but attack elections and courts; split.

direct-votes.rationale: Populist but no stated referendum doctrine; split.

workers-councils.rationale: Implied: allies sought to criminalise support for communism, so council-based socialist power is rejected.

natural-rulers.rationale: Authoritarian leader cult but also anti-elite populism; split.

political-violence-never.rationale: His 2018 speech threatened to purge or kill "reds" and supporters attacked institutions on January 8, so many adherents accept it.

war-builds-character.rationale: Militarist but no stated position on war as character-building.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He said the state is Christian but later promised to keep it secular; split.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Strong militarism and state security preclude privatized defense.

military-superiority.rationale: Militarism is a component, though no source states rivalry goals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Brazilian nationalism is not framed ethnically in sources; inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Implied by its staunch anti-communism; the Marxist view of history is not discussed directly.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Implied by his opposition to racial quotas and affirmative action, which he sees as dividing society.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: It rolled back Indigenous protection and stripped FUNAI of demarcation power.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from his opposition to racial quotas as dividing society; colonial reparations are not discussed.

civilizational-union.rationale: Nationalist anti-globalism; though it built a far-right transnational network, no civilizational union claim.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Evangelical meritocratic prosperity theology and ultraliberalism legitimize individual striving.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Emphasis on family, order and patriotism suggests it, but not explicit.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Indifference to deforestation and mining on protected land.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Implied by his support for agribusiness, opening the Renca Amazon reserve to mining and expanding hydroelectric and nuclear power.

algorithmic-government.rationale: No stated position; traditionalist and personalist leadership suggests no.

restore-past-order.rationale: Scholars call its political-cultural orientation reactionary, and Bolsonaro praised the 1964-85 dictatorship.

results-over-ideology.rationale: It is strongly ideological (anticommunism, culture war), despite pragmatic coalition-building.

direct-action.rationale: Contests elections as vehicle but supporters sought a coup; split leaning no.

means-match-ends.rationale: Sources document no doctrine on prefigurative means; the movement's means were electoral and confrontational.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Implied by his pro-development stance on mining, agribusiness and Amazon power projects; foraging is never discussed.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Implied by its anti-communism and market liberalism; the division of labour is not discussed.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Implied: the movement's economic liberalism and anti-communist motto that the flag will never be red reject communist distribution.

production-for-use.rationale: Implied by its neoliberal economics and the plan's privatisation drive, which treat profit-making firms as the engine of growth.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Implied by its pro-business liberalism and anti-communism; the exploitation thesis is not discussed.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Implied by its staunch anti-communism, including allied bills to criminalise support for communism.

collective-farming.rationale: Opposed land reform and defends rural property.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Implied by its embrace of market liberalism and rejection of communist doctrine; theories of imperialism are not discussed.

taxation-theft.rationale: Calls for lower taxes but the plan keeps a state tax system; split.

harm-principle.rationale: Moral conservatism restricts drugs, abortion and same-sex marriage beyond harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Opposes group rights like quotas but also emphasizes family; split.

conscription.rationale: Militarism suggests acceptance; no stated position.

state-as-business.rationale: Pro-privatization but not explicitly customer-citizen doctrine.

media-academia-power.rationale: Bolsonarism distrusts the media and sought to dismantle bodies such as the Oswaldo Cruz Foundation that it called dens of leftism, implying it sees them as an unelected rival power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not a stated doctrine; scholars link racism to the movement but adherents deny.

total-state.rationale: Economic liberal plan rejects total state direction.

national-rebirth.rationale: The movement frames Brazil as freeing itself from socialism and rescuing the country from corruption.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Cult of personality but no feudal oath doctrine.

bound-labor.rationale: Plan favours freer individual labor contracts.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Scientific denialism notwithstanding, adherents accuse the left of ideological bias and claim truth; relativism is rejected.

universal-morality.rationale: Christian values presented as universal truths.

single-common-good.rationale: Moral-unanimity rhetoric ("Brazil above everything"), but not stated.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He advocates close ties with Israel; evangelical base supports it.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No source documents a Bolsonarista position on diaspora return; neutral by default.

school-vouchers.rationale: Market-friendly education reform; inferred, also "homeschooling" push.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The plan sets a primary surplus goal and attacks past fiscal mismanagement.

economic-freedom.rationale: The economic program and anti-communism tie freedom to markets.

rule-by-example.rationale: No documented position; leadership is justified by popular mandate and the leader cult, not an ethic of moral example alone.

force-without-un.rationale: Anti-UN stance but no explicit military-use doctrine.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Implied by its defence of Christian values and association with scientific denialism.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Meritocratic ideology and pro-work welfare design; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Aligned with the US and Israel, not anti-Western.

workers-nation.rationale: Anti-left; nationalist but no labor doctrine.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Traditional family values and opposition to feminism; weaker as law.

ban-interest.rationale: Implied by the plan's orthodox financial programme with an independent central bank; interest is not discussed.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Implied: he opposes racial quotas as dividing society, and no source shows support for legal segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Implied: the Marxist theory of the state is not discussed, but the movement rejects communist doctrine wholesale.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Opposes immigration; also favoured assimilating Indigenous peoples.

elite-replacement.rationale: No documented Great Replacement doctrine; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: Sources report no stance on electoral systems; adherents are not split along this line in any documented way.

national-mission.rationale: Nationalism is inward-facing ("Brazil above everything"); no documented mission to export Brazil's system.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Implied: Bolsonarism blames feminist movements for moral chaos rather than accepting their account of structural patriarchy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The plan promised governing without backroom deals and named corruption as a priority; anti-political rhetoric is core.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not a doctrine; Christian family values oppose.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Bolsonaro praised the dictatorship and said torture was legitimate.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Liberal economics but strong security and moral state; split.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not a doctrine of the movement.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Formally professes governing for everyone, though sources document hostile rhetoric about groups.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Inferred: an intra-socialist debate the sources never touch; as anti-communists they reject the premise of building socialism at all.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred from its nationalist pride in Brazil and opposition to Indigenous land reserves; the colonial-project thesis is not discussed.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not an issue in Brazil, which already has one civil code; no stance documented.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Evangelical base prizes proselytizing freedom; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Opposes secularism; school religion favoured by evangelical base.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Inferred: this Stalinist thesis is never discussed, and anti-communists oppose any socialist state growing stronger.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Claims popular legitimacy while contesting election results; split.

trade-surplus.rationale: Pro-trade deals but no mercantilist doctrine.

population-transfer.rationale: No documented policy of expelling minorities; Brazilian nationalism is not framed that way, so inferred negative.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Allies proposed criminalizing communism, but sees such bans as abused against them; split.

separated-powers.rationale: Formally professed but attacks on STF and Congress show tension; split.

vanguard-party.rationale: Implied by Bolsonaro's description of the São Paulo Forum as a communist group led by Lula and Castro, an enemy rather than a model.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Evangelical charity rhetoric but market orientation; split.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: No documented position on population as cause of poverty; neutral by default.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Opposition to immigration and quotas but no explicit claim; split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Hostile to anything beyond electoral competition.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Bolsonaro planned a self-coup and threatened internal enemies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The plan blames dirigismo for inflation.

party-controls-media.rationale: It attacks the media as leftist but seeks private pluralism, not a ruling-party monopoly.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: No documented position; the plan targets corruption rather than politicians' pay scales.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Bolsonaro changed parties repeatedly and the movement is personalist, so binding party discipline is not a documented tenet.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Implied by its opposition to globalism; supranational union is not discussed.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not applicable; evangelical base is congregational.

clerical-rule.rationale: Though religious, the movement works through electoral politics.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Implied by its militarism and patriotism; revolutionary defeatism is not discussed.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Moral-chaos framing suggests it; the movement also claims to oppose censorship, so split.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: No documented stance; Bolsonaro sought re-election within the existing single-reelection rule.

recall-officials.rationale: No documented stance on recall; neutral by default.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Favoured alignment with the US and Israel.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Implied by the plan's call to remove any qualification of private property from the Constitution; rental housing is not discussed.

people-in-arms.rationale: Gun-rights advocacy; wants citizens armed for self-defense, but professional army remains.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Agribusiness base but no stated claim.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Brazil has no divided-nation question; the issue is not addressed by the movement.

death-penalty.rationale: He defended the death penalty even though Brazil's 1988 Constitution bans it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: He opposed the "gay kit" and blames schools for children's sexuality views.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: No documented stance; Brazil uses birthright citizenship and the movement does not campaign on changing it.

religious-exemptions.rationale: No documented stance on exemptions for minorities; evangelical priorities concern the majority faith, so neutral.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Traditionalism and attacks on non-conforming lifestyles.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The plan is fiscally orthodox, committing to pay down public debt and run surpluses, so cancellation is rejected.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Praised the dictatorship but no stated trade-off doctrine; split.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: No documented stance; Brazil has renounced nuclear weapons and the movement has not challenged this.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Populist presidential movement relying on direct vote.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The plan keeps the central bank formally independent.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not applicable to Brazil; no documented stance on territorial peace deals.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The plan sought to strip qualification of property rights from the Constitution.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Treats USSR as communist; no stated stance on the question.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Implied by his rejection of the climate consensus and plans to open Amazon reserves to mining.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: No documented stance on annexations; foreign policy focus is alignment with the US and Israel.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Implied by his opposition to state secularism and his claim that the state is Christian.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Personal party leadership by the president.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from its militarism and nationalism; secession is not discussed.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Cult of the "myth" but not divine descent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Plan simplifies taxes and cuts but also negative income tax; split.

character-from-environment.rationale: Meritocratic and religious view of individual agency; inferred.

space-expansion.rationale: No documented position; not part of the movement's agenda.

mixed-constitution.rationale: No documented position on classical constitutional theory; neutral by default.

leader-cult.rationale: The movement's "myth" cult around Bolsonaro is documented.

equal-parenting.rationale: No documented position on custody presumptions; family-values rhetoric leaves it unclear, so neutral.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred: a Maoist thesis about socialist societies that the sources never discuss; the anti-communist movement rejects its premises.

land-redistribution.rationale: He opposed land reforms, and the 2018 plan proposed treating land invasions as terrorism.

refugee-return.rationale: No documented stance on refugee return; its immigration stance concerns arrivals, not return.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: No such claim in Brazilian nationalism.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred: punishing apostasy is not discussed, and his evangelical base relies on freedom to convert.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred: dress-code law is not discussed; the movement defends traditional roles through Christian values, not covering laws.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not an issue the movement addresses; neutral by default.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Implied by its anti-communism and emphasis on Christian values and moral decline over economic causes.

no-bailouts.rationale: Liberal doctrine suggests but no source; split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: It contests the STF and electoral courts as against the people's will.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Implied by its hostility to feminist movements; parity quotas for women are not discussed.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Supports trade deals and open ties.

moral-incentives.rationale: Implied by its market liberalism; the Guevarist idea of moral incentives is not discussed.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Argues for lower inheritance taxes; not on titles.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Assimilationist toward Indigenous but no stated colonial doctrine; split.

patriotic-education.rationale: Patriotism is a core theme and Bolsonaro's motto was that the flag will never be red, which implies schools should instil national pride.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: He criticised the racial quota system in Brazilian universities as a way of dividing society.

public-money-creation.rationale: Implied by the plan's independent central bank and primary surplus target; money creation is not discussed.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Brazil's predecessor empire is not invoked in documented Bolsonarista foreign policy, so inferred negative.

delink-world-market.rationale: He supported the EU-Mercosur free trade agreement and stayed in Mercosur while criticising it for putting ideology before economics.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: the movement rejects Marxist theories of exploitation and imperialism, but this thesis is never discussed.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Economic liberalism and property emphasis, but moral conservatism; split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Defends constitution formally but contests the 1988 constitution on death penalty; split.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: No documented stance; the movement does not engage with colonial treaties, so neutral.

elective-rulers.rationale: Bolsonarism contests power through elections and claims popular mandate, though it disputed the 2022 result.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Adherents claim the courts broke the constitution; split.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: No documented position; agribusiness-friendly outlook offsets any welfare concerns, so neutral.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Evangelical charity but no stated position.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Implied: Bolsonarism is a mass movement built around electoral campaigns and street mobilisation.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not a libertarian-pacifist doctrine; the movement endorses forceful policing and threatened force against political opponents.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Pro-market program with no interest in transforming the property system; the framing is a left-nationalist one it opposes.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: It claims constitutional legitimacy and professes respect for law, though critics note its disregard for court rulings; no doctrine of a ruler above law.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Militarism is a defining component, with army officers in key posts and appeals to the military during the 2022 crisis.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: Bolsonaristas blame media and culture for spreading left-wing ideas, not for pacifying people into accepting the existing order.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: the movement's hostility to the press, universities and 'globalism' rests on the idea that elites rule through cultural institutions.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred: the ultraliberal Guedes agenda favours trade opening and foreign investment; its anti-globalism is about sovereignty, not unequal exchange.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from the movement's nationalism and restrictive immigration positions; not stated as a programme item.

party-own-road.rationale: Bolsonarism is anti-socialist and has no stance on how communist parties should coordinate; it is truly indifferent.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred: the 2018 plan stressed privatisation and openness to markets and investment rather than autarkic development.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Brazil has no live territorial grievance and the movement's foreign policy is not irredentist; inferred disagreement.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Bolsonaro opposed new indigenous land demarcation and favoured integrating indigenous peoples into national society.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from the movement's hostility to the left and antifa-style activism and its sympathy for the military regime.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: strong anti-communism leads Bolsonaristas to condemn communist totalitarianism and to cast Nazism as left-wing, which accepts the pairing.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A US-specific historical debate that the movement has not addressed; adherents have no documented position.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the movement's defence of the military regime's legacy and of national symbols against left-wing revisionism.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from the movement's anti-feminism and rejection of 'gender ideology', which resists programmes aimed only at women.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from the same anti-feminist stance; sceptical of gender-specific protection framing, though not stated in the sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred: Bolsonarism presents itself as defending Western Judeo-Christian civilization and an Atlanticist alignment, not civilizational pluralism.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred: ultraliberal fiscal austerity and conservative family values oppose wages for domestic work.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the evangelical-backed, traditional-family moral conservatism described in the overview.

office-by-exam.rationale: Split: Bolsonaro courted civil-service reform yet appointed many military officers and allies by discretion.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from nationalism and Bolsonaro's statements about keeping strategic assets such as niobium from Chinese buyers.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from religious social conservatism, though Brazil already has no-fault divorce and it is not a campaign issue.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred: the movement centres on a strong leader, not instructed delegates, and defends fixed terms.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The 2018 government plan proposed introducing a system of individual capitalisation accounts in place of pay-as-you-go; Congress later dropped it, so the support is qualified.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Strong anti-communism and defence of rural property make adherents hostile to land held in common or by use, such as the landless movement's claims.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred: adherents accept constitutional budget approval, though Bolsonaro often clashed with Congress over it.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from the nationalism and integration stance toward Indigenous peoples in his documented positions.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Split: nationalist suspicion of foreign land purchases conflicts with agribusiness allies who want foreign investment.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Bolsonaro opposed racial quotas and treats discrimination as individual, intentional conduct.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from ultraliberal economics, which defends consumption, and a moral-conservative streak that pulls weakly the other way.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the sovereignty emphasis and non-interventionist foreign policy, though hostile to leftist governments.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the nationalism and sovereignty emphasis; no source states a doctrine of intervention in allies.

corporate-influence.rationale: Its ultraliberal economics tolerates business interests and the movement does not campaign against lobbying; inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The movement's hostility to 'globalism' and foreign NGOs in the Amazon points toward limits on foreign funding; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Moral conservatism and family emphasis suggest support for pro-family incentives, though no source states it.

residents-only-property.rationale: The 2018 plan treated private property as fundamental, so limiting purchases to residents cuts against it; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Economic liberalism and labour deregulation oppose state employer-of-last-resort schemes; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: The movement has no doctrine on democracy promotion; it is pro-US but sceptical of multilateralism.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Order, tough policing and militarism leave little room for a right to disobey; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: It defends Brazilian sovereignty over the Amazon but backs allies abroad; adherents are split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Its labour reform and hostility to the left and unions make union organising by industry unlikely; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Its conspiracies centre on communists, the left and globalists, not an ethnic or religious minority; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Evangelical-backed moral conservatism defends traditional marriage; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: No source documents a position; the government was criticised over secrecy yet adherents back open records against the left.

local-production.rationale: Ultraliberal, export-oriented agribusiness favours free trade over local production; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: It is a personalist movement built around a leader, mass media and party structures, not small informal groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Anti-globalism and withdrawal from or hostility to international bodies favour national sovereignty over international courts.

religious-nation.rationale: The evangelical wing is influential but the movement defines Brazil by nation and family, so adherents are split.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Bolsonarism stressed national sovereignty yet aligned with the United States; inferred, not stated.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: No documented position on regional revenue sharing; inferred as indifferent.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Anti-communism and the defence of property as fundamental rule out common ownership; inferred.

defeat-communism.rationale: Strong anti-communism and hostility to the left are defining features of the movement.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The 2018 plan's privatisation agenda favours private providers, so a mild yes is inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Evangelical-backed moral conservatism makes religion central, not an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Ultraliberal economic thinking treats capitalism as the engine of prosperity.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Reactionary culture politics opposes feminism and structural reform; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Ultraliberal austerity opposes expanding public services; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not a documented concern of the movement; inferred as indifferent.

treaties-binding.rationale: Bolsonaro opposed new indigenous land demarcations, implying treaties and demarcations should be revisable; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Commune-based common property conflicts with anti-communism and property rights; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: No documented position on steering majority settlement; inferred as indifferent.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Bolsonarism is capitalist and anti-communist, so a third way is not its aim; inferred.

missingStatements.text: The armed forces should play a political role as guardians of order and the constitution.
missingStatements.rationale: Militarism is a defining component, with army officers in key posts and appeals to the military during the 2022 crisis.

missingStatements.text: Governments should lower the age of criminal responsibility.
missingStatements.rationale: The 2018 plan proposed lowering the age of criminal responsibility to 16.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow criminal-justice policy detail from one platform; the tough-on-crime stance is already captured by rehabilitation and empower-police-military.

missingStatements.text: Occupying private land or property as a protest should be treated as terrorism.
missingStatements.rationale: The 2018 plan classified land and property invasions as terrorism.

notes: Many answers are low-confidence inferences because Bolsonarism is a personalist movement with limited doctrine on abstract questions. Strands: the economic-liberal wing, the evangelical wing and the military wing weigh differently.
